prompt_text: AI to draft donor thank you letters
response_text:
You can use AI both to **generate individual donor thank you letters on demand** and to **automate the whole acknowledgment workflow** from your CRM. Below are practical options and ready-to-use prompts you can copy/paste into ChatGPT or a similar tool.

---

## 1. Use a strong prompt to draft better thank you letters

Tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Poe, etc. will do most of the work if you feed them a clear prompt that bakes in fundraising best practices.[1][3]

### Core reusable prompt (customize the [brackets])

Paste this into your AI tool and fill in the brackets:

> You are an experienced nonprofit fundraising and donor stewardship professional.  
>  
> Draft a warm, specific, 1-page thank you letter to **[donor name or “a recent donor”]** who gave **[gift amount or description]** to support **[program / designation]** at **[organization name]**.  
>  
> Organization context:  
> - Mission and vision: **[1–3 sentences]**  
> - Key programs and current impact: **[3–5 bullets with brief stats or outcomes]**  
> - Tone: **[e.g., warm and upbeat / professional and heartfelt / formal but friendly]**  
>  
> Letter requirements:  
> 1. Start with a creative, human opening line that immediately shows genuine gratitude (no “On behalf of” and no “Dear Friend”).  
> 2. Use first person (“I” and “we”) and second person (“you”) frequently.  
> 3. Clearly explain how this specific gift will be used and what *impact* the donor is making, using details from the context.  
> 4. If information is provided about past giving, acknowledge their ongoing support.  
> 5. If it’s a tribute gift (“in honor of / in memory of”), mention that with appropriate sensitivity.  
> 6. Avoid jargon like “we are deeply grateful for your continued support” and generic phrases.  
> 7. Keep the letter concise, warm, and easy to read. Use contractions (we’re, you’ll) and light emotion; a few exclamation marks are okay but don’t overuse them.  
> 8. Do **not** ask for another gift or include any fundraising ask. This letter is only for gratitude and acknowledgment.  
> 9. Include this tax language near the end: **[paste your IRS/CRA/legal acknowledgment sentence]**.  
> 10. Close with a personal sign-off from **[name, title, phone/email if desired]**.  

This incorporates best-practice elements from fundraising experts like the Gail Perry Group and prompt frameworks designed for donor letters.[1][3]

### Example: fast “fill-in-the-blanks” version

> Write a short, warm, upbeat thank you letter to **[donor name]** for their gift of **[amount or “your generous contribution”]** to **[organization]**, which will be used for **[specific purpose]**.  
>  
> Start with a creative sentence that charms the donor and shows real gratitude. Use “I/we” and “you” a lot. Explain the impact of their gift in concrete terms (“Because of your gift, a family will…”). Use contractions, show some emotion, and avoid formal phrases like “on behalf of” or “we are deeply grateful for your continued support.” Don’t ask for anything else. Sign it from **[name, role, phone/email]**.[1]

Use this for quick, single letters; use the longer prompt when you need more nuance.

---

## 2. Improve quality with better inputs

AI only works as well as the context you provide.[2][3]

Feed in:

- **Donor details:** name, gift date/amount, designation, first-time or repeat, tribute info.  
- **Your mission & programs:** short descriptions and 2–3 current impact stats.[2][3]  
- **Past examples:** upload or paste one or two *good* past letters so the AI can mirror your voice.[3]  
- **Any required language:** tax wording, disclaimers, or branding phrases.[2]

Prompts like those from AI for Education and Gail Perry encourage you to explicitly connect your mission and vision to the donor’s gift and impact, which usually produces stronger letters.[1][3]

---

## 3. If you want automation (not just one-off letters)

If your goal is “we get a donation → AI drafts a letter → it’s sent or queued for review,” you can set up an automated workflow with a platform like OpenClaw, Zapier, or an AI-enabled CRM.[2][9]

A typical setup looks like this:[2]

1. **Trigger**  
   - New donation recorded in your CRM or form.

2. **Context gathering**  
   - Pull donor name, amount, designation, giving history, notes, event attendance, tribute info, etc.[2]

3. **Segmentation logic**  
   - Example tiers:  
     - Tier 1: Small gifts → short email, auto-send.  
     - Tier 2: Mid-level → richer email or letter, auto-send.  
     - Tier 3: Major gifts → AI draft, *must* be reviewed/edited by staff before sending.[2]

4. **Letter generation**  
   - Use a *system prompt* for the agent, such as the framework below, then pass in the donor data.[2]

5. **Routing & delivery**  
   - Auto-send emails for lower tiers; route drafts to staff for higher tiers; store the final letter/PDF back in CRM.[2]

6. **Logging & next steps**  
   - Log that acknowledgment was sent and schedule a follow-up task (call, meeting, impact report, etc.).[2]

---

## 4. Example system prompt for an AI “thank you agent”

From the OpenClaw example, adapted:[2]

> You are a donor stewardship specialist for **[Organization Name]**.  
> Your job is to write warm, specific, genuine thank-you letters to donors.  
>  
> Organization context:  
> - [Organization Name] is a **[type of org]** serving **[population/mission]**.  
> - Our tone is **[warm and professional / casual and heartfelt / formal and distinguished]**.  
> - Our Executive Director is **[Name]**.  
> - Current key programs: **[3–5 programs with 1-sentence descriptions]**.  
> - Current impact stats: **[e.g., “served 1,200 students this year,” “planted 50,000 trees”]**.  
>  
> Rules:  
> 1. Always use the donor’s preferred name from their record.  
> 2. Reference their specific gift designation, not just the amount.  
> 3. If they are a repeat donor, acknowledge their history and loyalty.  
> 4. If tribute information is present, mention it with appropriate sensitivity.  
> 5. Include this required tax acknowledgment language: **[insert exact sentence]**.  
> 6. Never fabricate impact stories; only reference programs and outcomes from the provided context.  
> 7. Match length and depth of the letter to the “gift tier” field in the input.  
> 8. Use a warm, human tone that feels like a real person wrote it.

This is the “brain” you’d configure in OpenClaw or a similar agent framework, which then handles incoming donation data.[2]

---

## 5. Dedicated AI tools you can explore

If you prefer off‑the‑shelf tools instead of building your own setup, there are several options focused on donor letters:

- **Fundwriter.ai** – Built for fundraising content; quickly drafts personalized donor thank you letters and appeals.[6]  
- **FreeWill “Thank you notes”** – Simple AI-powered thank you note generator for nonprofit pros (prompts you for donor + org details).[7]  
- **Taskade Donor Thank-You Letter Generator** – Guided AI generator that helps produce personalized letters.[8]  
- **DonorPerfect AI writer bot** – If you use DonorPerfect, its AI tools can help personalize outreach and donor engagement.[9]  
- **Poe / custom GPTs** – There is at least one free “fundraiser thank you letter” assistant you can access via Poe or GPT that asks questions then generates a reusable thank-you template where you can swap donor details.[4]

Most of these ask for your org name, mission, type of contribution, and impact details, then create customizable drafts in seconds.[4][5][6][7][8]

---

If you tell me your organization’s mission, typical donor types, and whether you want one-off letters or a full automation, I can draft a tailored master prompt plus 2–3 ready-made templates you can start using immediately.
